"Today, we took a new step forward as Finland joined the French forward deterrence initiative. The initiative is first and foremost about strengthening European security," Finnish President Alexander Stubb posted on X . "It reinforces Europe’s responsibility for its own defence and helps prevent escalation." The Nordic country's decision is the latest example of Europeans rethinking their defense posture amid Russia’s escalating hybrid attacks across the continent and doubts about the reliability of U.S. security guarantees. Finland joined NATO in 2023 after decades of neutrality, and its embrace of closer European defense cooperation reflects how Russia’s war against Ukraine has reshaped Europe's security architecture. stories.title: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
stories.summary: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MVpi Roma artist Norbert Olah in the Bura Galeria in Budapest Image: Tobias Zuttmann/DW Advertisement The painting on the canvas is of a man playing chess with a robot. The color on his face is still damp and glistening. Norbert Olah was working into the early hours: The Bura Galeria in Budapest has been his studio all summer. He finds it easiest to concentrate at night, when the Hungarian capital gradually falls silent. Olah has taped foil and cardboard over the tiled floor at the back of the gallery. Pots of brushes, tubes of paint, pencil sketches, and, over and over again, pictures that include the blue-and-green Roma flag line the room. Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he deliberately left this part of his identity out of his art. Not because his ethnicity wasn't important to him, but because he didn't want to be labeled a "Romani artist."
